\chapter{Six, Seven, Eight, Nine}
\label{ch:mr-six-to-nine}
\hlchaptermodality{55}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can count from six to nine, four numbers further than the book has taken me since chapter thirteen.}

Complete MR-R55-six-to-nine and count from ek to nau without stopping -- four numbers more than chapter thirteen left you with.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[sahā]{\mr{सहा} (sahā) — six}

\label{lesson:MR-C55-saha}



\begin{quote}
Count \textbf{\mr{एक} \mr{दोन} \mr{तीन} \mr{चार} \mr{पाच}} and stop. Since chapter thirteen that has been the whole of what you can count.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{सहा}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{सहा}} — \emph{sahā} — \textbf{6}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{षष्}} (\emph{ṣaṣ}) is the ancestor, and it is the same word as Latin \emph{sex} and English \textbf{six}. The opening consonant softened on its way into Marathi; everything else is recognisably there.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahā chahā} — six teas
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek don tīn chār pāch sahā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{thoḍaṁ pāṇī} — a little water
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{lahān khoolī} — and no ending on it
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is six in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{सहा}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%B8\%E0\%A4\%B9\%E0\%A4\%BE}{Wiktionary: \mr{सहा}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sāt]{\mr{सात} (sāt) — seven}

\label{lesson:MR-C55-saat}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{सहा}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{सात}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{सात}} — \emph{sāt} — \textbf{7}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{सप्त}} (\emph{sapta}), which is Latin \emph{septem} and English \textbf{seven}. The \textbf{\mr{प}} dropped out and the \textbf{\mr{त}} stayed, and that collapse is the single most common thing that happened to these words on their way from Sanskrit.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāt} — seven
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahā} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{puresaṁ} — enough
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{sundar} — beautiful
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kā?} — why?
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is seven in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{सात}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%B8\%E0\%A4\%BE\%E0\%A4\%A4}{Wiktionary: \mr{सात}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āṭh]{\mr{आठ} (āṭh) — eight}

\label{lesson:MR-C55-aath}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{सात}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{आठ}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{आठ}} — \emph{āṭh} — \textbf{8}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{अष्ट}} (\emph{aṣṭa}) — Latin \emph{octo}, English \textbf{eight}. Hear what the \textbf{\mr{ष्ट}} became: a single retroflex \textbf{\mr{ठ}}. That is the regular outcome, and it is why so many Marathi words carry a retroflex where Sanskrit had a cluster.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āṭh} — eight
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahā sāt} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{baraṁch} — quite a lot
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kāraṇ …} — because …
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is eight in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{आठ}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%86\%E0\%A4\%A0}{Wiktionary: \mr{आठ}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[naū]{\mr{नऊ} (naū) — nine}

\label{lesson:MR-C55-nau}



\begin{quote}
Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{आठ}} and stop. The book has taken you no further than that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{नऊ}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{नऊ}} — \emph{naū} — \textbf{9}
\end{quote}

Sanskrit \textbf{\mr{नव}} (\emph{nava}) — Latin \emph{novem}, English \textbf{nine}. And \textbf{\mr{नव}} also meant \textbf{new}, in Sanskrit exactly as \emph{novem} and \emph{novus} are a pair in Latin. Nine is the new number: the one that starts the count over after eight.

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naū} — nine
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahā sāt āṭh} — the run up to it, without looking
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kitī sundar!} — how beautiful!
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{chāṅglā chahā} — good tea
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{chahā, dūdh āṇi pāṇī} — with the comma doing the joining
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is nine in Marathi? (\textbf{\mr{नऊ}}.) Say the number before it, and the one before that.

Sources: \href{https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%A4\%A8\%E0\%A4\%8A}{Wiktionary: \mr{नऊ}}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sahā · sāt · āṭh · naū]{Four numbers past five}

\label{lesson:MR-R55-six-to-nine}



\begin{quote}
Four numbers landed in this chapter. Count from \textbf{\mr{एक}} to \textbf{\mr{नऊ}} without stopping.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek don tīn chār pāch sahā sāt āṭh naū} — one to nine
  \item \emph{Say it:} the four new ones alone — \emph{sahā sāt āṭh naū}
  \item \emph{Say it:} which of the four carries a retroflex — \emph{\textbf{\mr{आठ}}}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kharāb pāṇī} — bad water
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How far can you count now? (\textbf{To nine}.) Which of the four is the same word as \emph{new}? (\textbf{\mr{नऊ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
